tasks.text: Send your written appeal to HR — the draft is ready in our chat. Deadline Tuesday 9/15.
tasks.why: The appeal asks for the internal-application ineligibility period (12/8) to be lifted. Filing inside the window is what counts — you can supplement with dates and corrected timecards afterwards. Review the draft, make it yours, send.

tasks.text: Email HR for the dates behind the 9/8 corrective action.
tasks.why: You cannot match absences to the certification without them. Ask: “Could you send me the attendance record behind the corrective action issued 9/8, including the specific dates and occurrences it is based on? I am preparing a written appeal within the seven-day window.” Naming the window tends to speed up the reply.

tasks.text: Submit Workday timecard corrections for any late arrivals the FMLA covers.
tasks.why: Absence Management's own email spells out the route: past pay periods go through a timecard correction request in Workday (see the Timecard Correction Job Aid attached). Current and future ones get coded ILL-1. Do this for every date that falls inside the certified frequency — a corrected timecard is the strongest possible evidence for the appeal.

tasks.text: 9/14 — APRN appointment: bring the ADA accommodation form + talking points for Q2–Q5.
tasks.why: The form is only useful if it comes back completed. Walk in with it and the Q2–Q5 talking points already written so nothing depends on remembering it in the room.

tasks.text: After 9/14 — Submit the completed ADA form to Absence Management.
tasks.why: Fax 216-444-7385, or email AMOforms@ccf.org. Dated paperwork going in is what starts the clock and protects you later.

tasks.text: After submission — Call Absence Management: ask about interim schedule flexibility while the accommodation is under review.
tasks.why: Review takes time, and you need the mornings to work in the meantime. Asking for interim flexibility is a separate, smaller ask than the accommodation itself.

Mon–Thu 8am–6pm, Fri 8am–5pm ET. Have your Z number ready. Ask: “I have a hold on my account — registration, financial aid, and transcript — from a Parent PLUS loan default. My mother is entering a loan rehabilitation agreement with the loan servicer. Does signing an active rehabilitation agreement release these holds, or does the loan need to be fully out of default first?”

tasks.text: Text the Senior Director at Weston.
tasks.why: ON HOLD until the appeal resolves — she cannot place you in this cohort while the 12/8 lockout stands, so there is nothing for her to act on yet. When it is time, put her name in first and send between 9am and 4pm. “Hi [Name] — it's Stacey Doret, just following up on the EEG apprentice application we spoke about. I know it's not a quick yes-or-no on your end — it sits with HR and has its own steps, and I appreciate you carrying it. No rush on a final answer — would it be alright if I checked back on the 17th?”

tasks.text: 9/17 — Follow up with the Senior Director if she hasn't come back to you.
tasks.why: Only if the appeal has resolved by then. If it has not, this waits — you go to her with your eligibility restored, or in late November about December. Open with “Circling back as promised —”.

tasks.text: FMLA — approved 9/9. Intermittent, no further paperwork from you.
tasks.why: Notice of Eligibility and Designation Notice both issued 9/9/2026. Going forward, intermittent absences get coded ILL-1 on the timecard; past pay periods go through Workday. Keep following your department's normal call-off procedure.

tasks.text: Put Mom’s $119 on a payment plan preferably the day after payday and for every two weeks
Make Lori do at least ONE session of grow therapy by the end of September 2026
